test_cases.test_name: Verify Continuous Temperature Monitoring and Recording Intervals
test_cases.objective: To verify that the Environmental Monitoring System continuously monitors temperature in GMP storage areas and records readings at intervals not exceeding 5 minutes.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are installed and calibrated in all GMP storage areas.
System access credentials are available.

test_steps.action: Log into the EMS system using valid credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: User is successfully logged into the EMS system.

test_steps.action: Navigate to the real-time monitoring screen for a designated GMP storage area.
test_steps.expected_result: Real-time temperature readings for the selected storage area are displayed.

test_steps.action: Observe the temperature readings and their timestamps for a period of at least 10 minutes.
test_steps.expected_result: Temperature readings are continuously updated, and the time difference between consecutive readings does not exceed 5 minutes.

test_steps.action: Access the historical data log for the same storage area and verify the recorded timestamps.
test_steps.expected_result: Historical data confirms that temperature readings were recorded at intervals not exceeding 5 minutes.

acceptance_criteria: The system continuously displays real-time temperature readings.
All recorded temperature data points have timestamps that are no more than 5 minutes apart.
data_integrity_requirements: Data is captured accurately and completely.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Temperature Alarm Generation and Notification Integration
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system generates alerts when temperature deviates ±2°C from setpoint and that alarm notifications integrate with the site paging system.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are installed and calibrated in all GMP storage areas.
A setpoint for temperature monitoring is defined.
Site paging system is configured and accessible for integration testing.
System access credentials are available.

test_steps.action: Log into the EMS system using valid credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: User is successfully logged into the EMS system.

test_steps.action: Identify a GMP storage area with a defined temperature setpoint and its acceptable deviation range (e.g., setpoint 20°C, deviation ±2°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The setpoint and deviation range for the selected storage area are clearly identified.

test_steps.action: Manually adjust the temperature in the selected storage area to exceed the upper deviation limit (e.g., > 22°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The temperature reading in the EMS system reflects the adjusted temperature.

test_steps.action: Observe the EMS system for alarm generation and verify the system response time.
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm is generated within 30 seconds of the temperature exceeding the deviation limit.

test_steps.action: Verify that an alarm notification is sent to the site paging system.
test_steps.expected_result: A notification is received on the designated paging system for the generated alarm.

test_steps.action: Manually adjust the temperature back within the acceptable range.
test_steps.expected_result: The temperature reading in the EMS system returns to within the acceptable range.

test_steps.action: Observe the EMS system for alarm deactivation and verify the status update.
test_steps.expected_result: The alarm status in the EMS system is updated to indicate the condition is resolved.

acceptance_criteria: Alarms are generated within 30 seconds when temperature deviates ±2°C from setpoint.
Alarm notifications are successfully sent to the site paging system.
Alarm status is correctly updated upon resolution.
data_integrity_requirements: Alarm events are accurately logged with correct timestamps.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Temperature Range Accuracy and Setpoint Deviation Alerts
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS accurately measures temperature within the specified range and generates alerts when deviations from the setpoint occur.
prerequisites: EMS is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are calibrated.
System is operational and logging data.

test_steps.action: Introduce a controlled temperature environment within the specified range (-80°C to +50°C) to a sensor and allow the EMS to record the reading.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS records the temperature reading within ±0.5°C of the actual controlled temperature.

test_steps.action: Set a specific temperature setpoint (e.g., 20°C) and then introduce a controlled temperature deviation of +2°C (to 22°C) to a sensor.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS generates an alert indicating a temperature deviation from the setpoint.

test_steps.action: Introduce a controlled temperature deviation of -2°C (to 18°C) from the same setpoint (20°C) to a sensor.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS generates an alert indicating a temperature deviation from the setpoint.

acceptance_criteria: All temperature readings are within ±0.5°C of the actual controlled temperature.
Alerts are generated for temperature deviations of ±2°C from the setpoint.
Alerts are logged with correct timestamps and deviation details.
data_integrity_requirements: Temperature readings are accurate and not tampered with.
Alerts are reliably generated and recorded.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Data Storage and Archival Functionality
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS stores all temperature data in the vendor's standard format and that the archival feature functions correctly for long-term retention.
prerequisites: EMS is installed and configured.
System is operational and logging data.
Sufficient data has been logged to test archival.

test_steps.action: Access the EMS database and verify that temperature readings are stored in the vendor's standard database format.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS data is stored in the expected vendor-supplied database format.

test_steps.action: Utilize the vendor's archival feature to archive historical data, simulating a 7-year retention period.
test_steps.expected_result: The archival process completes successfully, and the data is moved to the designated archive location.

test_steps.action: Attempt to retrieve data from the archived location to confirm its integrity and accessibility.
test_steps.expected_result: Archived data can be successfully retrieved and is consistent with the original data.
data_to_capture: Comparison of retrieved data with original data

acceptance_criteria: All logged data is stored in the vendor's standard database format.
The archival process successfully archives data for the specified retention period.
Archived data is retrievable and maintains its integrity.
data_integrity_requirements: Data is stored in an unalterable, vendor-standard format.
Archived data is secure, retrievable, and maintains its integrity over the retention period.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Vendor Software Integrity and Data Storage Format
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system utilizes vendor-supplied software without modification and stores data in the vendor's standard database format.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and operational.
Access to system logs and configuration files is available.
Documentation of vendor-supplied software version is available.

test_steps.action: Access the EMS system configuration and review software version information.
test_steps.expected_result: The system displays the vendor-supplied software version, matching the documented version.

test_steps.action: Generate a sample data report from the EMS.
test_steps.expected_result: The generated report is in the vendor's standard database format (e.g., CSV, SQL dump).

test_steps.action: Examine system logs for any indications of unauthorized software modifications.
test_steps.expected_result: No unauthorized modifications or custom code are detected in the system logs.

acceptance_criteria: The system is confirmed to be running the vendor-supplied software without any modifications.
All generated data reports are confirmed to be in the vendor's standard database format.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-003: The system shall use vendor-supplied software without modification.
URS-EMS-006: All data shall be stored in the vendor's standard database format.
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be stored in a format that is auditable and retrievable.
Software integrity is crucial to prevent data manipulation.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Electronic Signature and Audit Trail Functionality
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system implements electronic signatures and maintains a comprehensive audit trail in compliance with 21 CFR Part 11.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and operational.
User accounts with appropriate permissions for electronic signatures are configured.
Access to audit trail logs is available.

test_steps.action: Perform an action requiring an electronic signature (e.g., approving a report, acknowledging an alarm).
test_steps.expected_result: The system prompts for and captures a valid electronic signature, including user ID, date, time, and reason for the signature.
data_to_capture: Electronic signature details (user, date, time, reason)

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail for the action performed in Step 1.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail accurately records the electronic signature event, including all required components (who, what, when, why).
data_to_capture: Audit trail log entry for the signature event
Confirmation of all required audit trail components

test_steps.action: Perform a system configuration change (e.g., adjust a setpoint).
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail records the configuration change, including the user, date, time, and the specific change made.
data_to_capture: Audit trail log entry for the configuration change

test_steps.action: Attempt to delete or modify an audit trail entry.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prevents deletion or modification of audit trail entries.
data_to_capture: Error message or system behavior confirmation

acceptance_criteria: Electronic signatures are captured correctly with all required elements.
The audit trail accurately and comprehensively logs all significant system events, including electronic signatures and configuration changes.
Audit trail entries are immutable and cannot be altered or deleted.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-008: System shall maintain an audit trail per 21 CFR Part 11.
URS-EMS-009: Electronic signatures shall use vendor's built-in functionality.
data_integrity_requirements: Audit trails must be secure, time-stamped, and unalterable.
Electronic signatures must be unique and attributable to an individual.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Availability and Planned Maintenance Exclusion
test_cases.objective: To verify that the Environmental Monitoring System meets the required availability of 99.5% excluding planned maintenance periods.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System is installed and operational.
Access to system logs and availability monitoring tools.
Schedule of planned maintenance activities is available.

test_steps.action: Monitor system uptime over a defined period (e.g., 30 days) using automated monitoring tools.
test_steps.expected_result: System uptime is recorded and accessible.

test_steps.action: Identify and document all periods of planned maintenance during the monitoring period.
test_steps.expected_result: All planned maintenance activities are clearly identified and documented.
data_to_capture: Dates and durations of planned maintenance

test_steps.action: Calculate the total system availability, excluding the duration of planned maintenance.
test_steps.expected_result: The calculated availability is greater than or equal to 99.5%.

acceptance_criteria: The calculated system availability, excluding planned maintenance, is >= 99.5%.
data_integrity_requirements: System uptime data must be accurate and verifiable.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Facility Management System Integration and Alarm Notification
test_cases.objective: To verify that the Environmental Monitoring System successfully interfaces with the existing facility management system and integrates alarm notifications with the site paging system via the vendor API.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System is installed and operational.
Facility Management System is operational and configured for integration.
Site paging system is operational.
Vendor API documentation for alarm notifications is available.
Test credentials for facility management system and paging system.

test_steps.action: Configure the EMS to send temperature data to the facility management system using standard protocols.
test_steps.expected_result: Data is successfully transmitted to the facility management system.
data_to_capture: Configuration settings for facility management system integration

test_steps.action: Simulate a temperature deviation that triggers an alarm condition in the EMS.
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm is generated within the EMS.

test_steps.action: Verify that the alarm notification is sent to the site paging system via the vendor API.
test_steps.expected_result: An alert is received on the designated paging system.

test_steps.action: Verify that the alarm notification on the paging system contains relevant information (e.g., location, temperature, deviation).
test_steps.expected_result: The paging system alert contains accurate and relevant alarm details.
data_to_capture: Content of the paging system alert

acceptance_criteria: Temperature data is successfully transmitted to the facility management system.
Alarm notifications are successfully sent to the site paging system via the vendor API.
Paging system alerts contain accurate and relevant alarm information.
data_integrity_requirements: Data transmitted to the facility management system must be accurate.
Alarm notification content must be accurate.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Vendor Provided Reports for Batch Release
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system generates standard reports as provided by the vendor for use in batch release processes.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and configured.
Sufficient historical temperature data exists for report generation.
Access to vendor-supplied reporting tools or interface.

test_steps.action: Access the reporting module of the EMS.
test_steps.expected_result: The reporting module is accessible and displays available report templates.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the reporting module interface.

test_steps.action: Select and generate a standard temperature monitoring report for a defined period (e.g., last 24 hours).
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates a report in the vendor's standard format, containing accurate temperature data for the selected period.

test_steps.action: Review the generated report for completeness and accuracy against recorded data.
test_steps.expected_result: The report accurately reflects the recorded temperature data, including any alarms or deviations within the specified period.
data_to_capture: Comparison of report data with raw data logs.

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully generates standard reports as provided by the vendor.
Generated reports are accurate and contain all relevant temperature monitoring data.
The format of the generated reports is consistent with vendor specifications.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 (indirectly, as reports are used for batch release)
data_integrity_requirements: Report data must be a true and accurate reflection of recorded data.
Report generation process must not alter original data.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Availability and Planned Maintenance Exclusion
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system meets the specified availability requirement of 99.5% and that planned maintenance periods are correctly excluded from availability calculations.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is operational.
System logs are accessible for review.
A schedule of planned maintenance activities is available.

test_steps.action: Obtain system uptime logs for a defined period (e.g., one month).
test_steps.expected_result: System uptime logs are retrieved, detailing periods of system operation and downtime.

test_steps.action: Identify any planned maintenance periods within the log period from the maintenance schedule.
test_steps.expected_result: Planned maintenance periods are clearly identified and documented.
data_to_capture: List of planned maintenance dates and durations.

test_steps.action: Calculate the total operational time and total downtime, excluding planned maintenance periods.
test_steps.expected_result: Accurate calculation of operational time and unplanned downtime is performed.
data_to_capture: Calculation sheet or report showing total operational time, total downtime, and planned maintenance duration.

test_steps.action: Calculate the system availability percentage using the formula: (Total Operational Time / (Total Operational Time + Total Unplanned Downtime)) * 100.
test_steps.expected_result: The calculated availability percentage is determined.

acceptance_criteria: The calculated system availability percentage is 99.5% or higher.
All planned maintenance periods are correctly excluded from the availability calculation.
System logs accurately reflect operational status.
data_integrity_requirements: System uptime logs must be accurate and complete.
